Recorded open thread 1g in `blueprint/inner-workspace-updates/open-threads.md`: the fix for workspaces created from a published template reading no version is now decided and built app-side, so the entry records what shipped, why the app side was chosen over the template or publish side (those reach only templates published after the change; the version read reaches every workspace the app can exec into), what stays open after it (the create-time label, and the publish-side tag push, now recorded not as a competing candidate but as the thing that would retire the fetch for every template published after it), and the three accepted costs -- a workspace that stays tagless re-fetches on every detection sweep, the read writes the `official` remote into the workspace's git config, and the fetch itself is a measured transfer rather than a ref write. It also records what those measurements bought: the fetch runs only where a release tag could name the workspace, and the read's own exec and fetch ceilings are sized for the transfer and kept under the sweep's interval.

It also corrects the claim that only an `update-self` run ever lands `minds-v*` tags in a workspace: the backup check script fetches them too, from the per-workspace backups route.
